description: Observed wildfire activity and fire-weather conditions in Yukon.

total-area-burned.label: Total area burned
total-area-burned.description: Area of Yukon mapped as burned by wildfire each year.
total-area-burned.definition: Annual total area within Yukon recorded as burned by wildfire.
total-area-burned.why_we_track_it: Area burned is one of the clearest measures of the amount of land directly affected by wildfire. It varies greatly from year to year, but long-term changes can reveal shifts in Yukon wildfire activity.
total-area-burned.limitations: Area burned is influenced by weather, fuels, ignition, suppression, access and individual extreme fire seasons. It should not be interpreted as a direct measure of climate alone.
total-area-burned.trend_method: Theil-Sen slope is used because annual wildfire and fire-weather indicators can be strongly influenced by individual extreme years. Kendall tau tests whether there is evidence of a consistent long-term trend. Significance is assessed at p < 0.05.

number-of-fires.label: Number of fires
number-of-fires.description: Number of mapped wildfires recorded in Yukon each year.
number-of-fires.definition: Annual count of wildfire records in the Yukon fire-history dataset.
number-of-fires.why_we_track_it: Fire counts show how often wildfires are recorded, complementing area burned because a year with many small fires can look very different from a year dominated by a few very large fires.
number-of-fires.limitations: Fire counts are influenced by lightning and human ignitions, detection, reporting and suppression practices as well as climate.
number-of-fires.trend_method: Theil-Sen slope is used because annual wildfire and fire-weather indicators can be strongly influenced by individual extreme years. Kendall tau tests whether there is evidence of a consistent long-term trend. Significance is assessed at p < 0.05.

fire-severity.label: Fire severity
fire-severity.description: Summer Daily Severity Rating across the eight-community station series used in the previous Yukon indicator.
fire-severity.definition: June-August Daily Severity Rating from WFM stations representing Whitehorse, Carmacks, Mayo, Dawson City, Haines Junction, Ross River, Watson Lake and Teslin.
fire-severity.source: Government of Yukon Wildland Fire Management station archive
fire-severity.why_we_track_it: Daily Severity Rating gives greater weight to severe fire-weather conditions and provides continuity with the fire-severity indicator used in the previous Yukon climate report.
fire-severity.limitations: DSR is calculated directly from Fire Weather Index and is therefore not independent evidence from FWI. This indicator is retained primarily for continuity with the earlier Yukon indicator.
fire-severity.trend_method: Theil-Sen slope is used because annual wildfire and fire-weather indicators can be strongly influenced by individual extreme years. Kendall tau tests whether there is evidence of a consistent long-term trend. Significance is assessed at p < 0.05.

fire-weather-index.label: Fire Weather Index
fire-weather-index.description: Severity of sustained fire-weather conditions during the fire season.
fire-weather-index.definition: Annual maximum 90-day running mean Fire Weather Index, summarized as the annual median across the fixed long-record WFM station panel.
fire-weather-index.source: Government of Yukon Wildland Fire Management (WFM) station archive
fire-weather-index.why_we_track_it: Fire Weather Index describes how weather affects potential fire behaviour. Sustained high values indicate prolonged periods when fires can become more difficult to control.
fire-weather-index.limitations: FWI describes fire-weather conditions, not actual fire occurrence. Ignitions, fuels, landscape conditions and suppression also influence what ultimately burns.
fire-weather-index.trend_method: Theil-Sen slope is used because annual wildfire and fire-weather indicators can be strongly influenced by individual extreme years. Kendall tau tests whether there is evidence of a consistent long-term trend. Significance is assessed at p < 0.05.

trend_method: Wildfire trends use Theil-Sen slope to estimate the rate of long-term change and Kendall tau to assess whether there is evidence of a consistent monotonic trend. These methods are less sensitive to unusually severe individual years than ordinary least squares. Statistical significance is assessed at p < 0.05.
